question: Backlog B45: when a contact law tells its two rings apart, so that the automaton fixes how each ring continues (RING-LAW-20261109-001A: nonlinear laws, or affine ones that cut a ring), do the lattice tori and their line networks still keep their contacts bound (A32) or at least needing both rings, and do they read their distance plainly?

public_inputs.library: ring_law_lib.py of RING-LAW-20261109-001A-P001 (on REROUTE-20261109-001B's reroute_lib), pysat's CaDiCaL for the exact decisions.
public_inputs.run: run.py in this folder, 16 worker processes.
public_inputs.family: Square, triangular and honeycomb n x n tori for n = 4, 5, 6 at g = 2, and their line networks: 18 networks. Every self-blind law (u, v), u on the ring through dart 2c: 256 laws for R1; law (12, 12) and the eight symmetric nonlinear laws u = v in {1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 11, 13, 14} for R2 and R3. One contact of each translation class stands for all; every ring is read.
public_inputs.readings: R1: whether the representative contacts bind both their rings at every lag (affine laws, exact from the row orbit) or at every lag to 6 (nonlinear laws, exact by SAT, stopping at the first lag that fails). R2: whether they need both rings at every lag to 64. R3: for every ring and representative contact, whether the plain first need comes at the light-cone lag. R2 and R3 are exact: a sampled pair of first rows (256 per ring) witnesses needing, and every lag not witnessed is decided by SAT.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the roster, the laws, the lags or the hypotheses after seeing results
primary_observable: For each network: the laws that see the routing and still bind (H1); for the eight nonlinear laws, needing to lag 64 (H2) and the late (ring, contact) pairs (H3), against law (12, 12).
cheapest_meaningful_control: Law (12, 12): blind, binding at every lag, the tori late and the line networks on time (REROUTE-20261109-001B, PLAIN-TIME-20261108-001B).
decision_or_followup_rule: Frozen hypotheses. H1: on every network read no law that sees the routing binds both rings at every lag read. H2: under each of the eight symmetric nonlinear laws every representative contact needs both its rings at every lag to 64. H3: under those laws every network read is on time. If H1 holds, native rings that every ring passes cost binding on these lattices, and rings that bind are declarations (A45). If H1 fails, the binding law's plain reading is read next. If H3 holds, the plain reading's failure on two-dimensional networks belongs to affine laws, and with H1 a plane read plainly costs binding.
stop_rule: Stop when every network of the roster has its readings.
nonclaims: Exploratory and finite: the roster only.
Binding of nonlinear laws is read to lag 6 and needing to lag 64; neither is read at every lag.
Self-blind laws and rule-60 rings only; two-time knots only (A30).
feasibility_disclosure: Before freezing, pilots (scratch, not kept): (1) the six linear elementary ring rules under nine linear laws on the square 3 x 3 to 5 x 5 tori and their line networks, persistence by row orbits: under laws that read one arriving cell no contact persisted, except all 18 of the 3 x 3 line network under rule 150 and law (6, 10); (2) every law on four shapes of two rings sharing two contacts, both routings, needing by full state maps to lag 40: every law that sees the routing with both rings passing needed both rings at every lag in both routings; (3) the plain reading under law (12, 12) and five nonlinear laws on the square 4 x 4 to 6 x 6 tori and their line networks by sampled witnesses, and by SAT for the pairs not witnessed under (8, 14) at n = 5 and (8, 8) at n = 4, 5, 6 and on the triangular and honeycomb 4 x 4 and 5 x 5 tori: no pair was late under the nonlinear laws, and (12, 12) gave its known late pairs; (4) binding on the square 4 x 4 torus for all 256 laws to lag 6 (contacts 0 and 1): no law that sees the routing bound, the nonlinear ones failing at lag 3 or 4; (5) timing of the heaviest readings (up to 55 s each). H1 to H3 were written from these pilots; the census reads the three lattices at three sizes and both groupings, most of it not read before.
